source.title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Does every weakly compactly generated Banach space admit a norming Markushevich basis? Here “weakly compactly generated” means that the space has a weakly compact subset whose linear span is dense, and a “norming Markushevich basis” means a fundamental total biorthogonal system whose biorthogonal functionals span a norming subspace of the dual.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (John–Zizler). Does every WCG Banach space admit a norming M-basis?
Both these problems have been recently solved in the negative [50, 53] and we shall give more details on this in Section 4.

accepted.question_text: If X is an Asplund Banach space and X admits a norming Markushevich basis, must X be weakly compactly generated?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4 (Godefroy). Let X be an Asplund Banach space with a norming M-basis. Must X be WCG?
Both these problems have been recently solved in the negative [50, 53] and we shall give more details on this in Section 4.

accepted.question_text: Let ρ:[ω₁]²→ω be an ordinal metric as in Proposition 4.8, let F_n(α)={ξ≤α:ρ(ξ,α)≤n}, let F_ρ={F_n(α): n<ω, α<ω₁}, and let K_ρ be the closure of F_ρ in the pointwise topology of {0,1}^{ω₁}. Does the Banach space C(K_ρ) admit a norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.13. Does the Banach space C(Kϱ) admit a norming M-basis?
Having fixed such a function ϱ: [ω1]2 → ω, for n < ω and α < ω1 we let Fn(α) := {ξ ⩽ α: ϱ(ξ, α) ⩽ n};

accepted.question_text: Let K be a scattered compact space such that C(K), the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on K, admits a norming Markushevich basis. Must K be Eberlein, that is, homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of a Banach space?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 (Godefroy’s problem for C(K) spaces). Let K be a scattered compact space such that C(K) admits a norming M-basis. Is K Eberlein?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a scattered compact space such that C(K) admits a countably norming Markushevich basis, meaning an M-basis whose countably supported functionals form a norming subspace of C(K)*. Must K be a Valdivia compact space?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.9. Let K be a scattered compactum such that C(K) admits a (countably) norming M-basis. Does it follow that K is Valdivia?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a scattered Valdivia compact space that contains a copy of the ordinal interval [0,ω₁]. Is there a bounded linear extension operator from C([0,ω₁]) to C(K)? More generally, does C([0,ω₁]) embed into C(K)?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.10. Let K be a scattered Valdivia compactum that contains [0, ω1]. Is there a linear extension operator from C([0, ω1]) to C(K)? More generally, does C([0, ω1]) embed into C(K)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the dual unit ball (B_{X*},w*) of a Banach space X is Valdivia. Must X be Plichko, meaning that X admits a countably norming Markushevich basis?
accepted.context_brief: Valdivia dual ball versus Plichko structure

evidence.quote: It seems to be still open if X must be Plichko under this assumption, [73].
However, it is not true that X must be 1-Plichko if (BX∗, w∗) is Valdivia, [73].

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X has a norming Markushevich basis and Z is a subspace of X, must Z also admit a norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. Let X be a Banach space with norming M-basis and Z be a subspace of X. Must Z admit a norming M-basis as well?

accepted.question_text: Does every subspace of ℓ₁(Γ), where Γ is an uncountable index set, admit a norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.5. Does every subspace of ℓ1(Γ), Γ uncountable, admit a norming M-basis?

accepted.question_text: If Z is a subspace of a Plichko Banach space X, must Z also be Plichko?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.6. Let Z be a subspace of a Plichko Banach space X. Must Z be Plichko?
Differently from the problem for norming M-bases, this problem has been solved and a negative answer follows from Kubiś’ results, [76, 77].

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space such that its bidual X** is Plichko. Must X itself be Plichko?
accepted.context_brief: Plichko structure inherited from the bidual

evidence.quote: Problem 6.8 ([71, Question 6.14]). Let X be a Banach space such that X∗∗ is Plichko. Must X be Plichko?

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a complemented subspace of a Plichko Banach space X. Must Z be Plichko?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.9. Let Z be a complemented subspace of a Plichko space X. Must Z be Plichko?

accepted.question_text: For an ordinal η, is the Banach space C([0,η]) Plichko only in the range η<ω₂? Equivalently, does every ordinal interval [0,η] with η≥ω₂ give rise to a non-Plichko function space C([0,η])?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.10 (Kalenda, [72]). Is C([0, η]) Plichko only for η < ω2?

accepted.question_text: Does C([0,ω₂]) embed into a Plichko Banach space?
accepted.context_brief: Embedding C([0,ω₂]) into a Plichko space

evidence.quote: Problem 6.11 ([72, 78]). Does C([0, ω2]) embed in a Plichko space?

accepted.question_text: If X has a norming Markushevich basis and Z is a complemented subspace of X, must Z admit a norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.12. Let X be a Banach space with norming M-basis and Z be a complemented subspace of X. Must Z admit a norming M-basis?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space. (1) If X has a norming Markushevich basis, must the dual ball (B_{X*},w*) be semi-Eberlein? (2) If (B_{X*},w*) is semi-Eberlein for every equivalent renorming of X, must X be a subspace of a weakly compactly generated Banach space? (3) Are the dual balls of C([0,ω₁]) and of C(K_ρ) semi-Eberlein?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.4. (1) Let X be a Banach space with norming M-basis. Must (BX∗, w∗) be semi-Eberlein? (2) Assume that (BX∗, w∗) is semi-Eberlein for every renorming of X. Is X a subspace of a WCG Banach space? (3) Are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) or C(Kϱ) semi-Eberlein?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a semi-Eberlein compact space. Is there a homeomorphic embedding φ:K→[-1,1]^Γ such that the finitely supported points φ(K)∩c₀₀(Γ) are dense in φ(K)? In particular, does this hold when K is scattered, when K is Eberlein or uniform Eberlein, when K is the specific compact space constructed in Theorem 4.7, or when K is the dual ball of a Banach space?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.6. Let K be a semi-Eberlein compactum. Is there a homeomorphic embedding φ: K → [−1, 1]Γ such that φ(K) ∩ c00(Γ) is dense in φ(K)? In particular, is the property true in the following cases? (1) K is scattered; (2) K is actually Eberlein, or even uniform Eberlein; (3) in particular, K is the compactum constructed in [50], see Theorem 4.7; (4) K is the dual ball of a Banach space.

accepted.question_text: Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compact space contain a copy of the ordinal interval [0,ω₂]?
accepted.context_brief: Large ordinals inside scattered semi-Eberlein compacta

evidence.quote: Problem 7.7. Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum contain a copy of [0, ω2]?

needs_review.question_text_raw: First, every Asplund generated WLD Banach space of density at most ω1 is WCG, [37]; hence the WCG and WLD classes coincide also for Asplund generated spaces (but it is open if the same result holds for higher densities).
